topIssues.body:
## Project / Coordination

- Project board: N/A - standalone contributor-compute initiative; add to a maintainer-selected board if desired.
- Parent tracker or epic: N/A - this issue is the launch card.
- Coordination Discussion: N/A.
- Suggested lane tag: eliza-computer-codex

## Scope

Launch `eliza.computer` from this monorepo as a minimal Vite site that turns spare agent compute into reviewable elizaOS contributions. Ship a downloadable/runnable skill that selects and finishes issues, reviews open PRs, adds missing tests/evidence/validation/screenshots/video, follows the repository claim and evidence workflow, and discloses the exact model used. Add a transparent GitHub-backed contribution leaderboard, Cloudflare Pages CI/CD, and the contribution/template changes needed to make model attribution durable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A bundled, validated, installable contribution skill handles issue-finishing and PR-review workflows safely.
- [ ] The skill enforces claims, sync/rebase, package guidance, scoped validation, real evidence, independent review, and model disclosure.
- [ ] A responsive, accessible Vite site explains the workflow, installs/downloads the skill, surfaces open work, and renders a transparent elizaOS/eliza leaderboard.
- [ ] Leaderboard scoring covers merged PRs, issue work, substantive comments/reviews, evidence, and model disclosure with anti-gaming caps and documented methodology.
- [ ] PR/issue contribution guidance records model provenance, including a human-only declaration path.
- [ ] Unit, integration, build, accessibility, responsive, and real browser E2E checks pass; desktop/mobile screenshots and an MP4 walkthrough are manually reviewed.
- [ ] Cloudflare Pages deployment and custom domain are configured and production is verified over HTTPS.
- [ ] CI/CD refreshes leaderboard data and deploys only validated builds.

## Evidence Plan

Keep every applicable row visible. Use `N/A - <reason>` only when a row truly does not apply.

- [ ] Screenshots or recording: before/current reference plus after desktop/mobile JPGs and full-flow MP4.
- [ ] Logs: browser console/network, build/test logs, GitHub data refresh, and Cloudflare deploy/HTTP verification.
- [ ] Real-LLM trajectories: forward-test the skill on real repository work and attach the model-named trajectory/output.
- [ ] Domain artifacts: packaged skill archive, generated leaderboard JSON, live Pages deployment, DNS/TLS response.
- [ ] CI or local commands: package tests/typecheck/lint/build/E2E plus repository verify after rebase.

## Claim / Status Notes

Claim will be posted before implementation. Production deploy and DNS are shared levers and will be claimed explicitly before mutation.

- Agent/tooling: Codex desktop agent with repository, GitHub, browser, and Cloudflare tooling.
- Human-only work: none at issue creation.

topIssues.title: fix(ci): fence Calendar typecheck behind Video declarations
topIssues.author: NubsCarson
topIssues.body:
# Problem

A clean GitHub runner can start `@elizaos/plugin-calendar#typecheck` while `@elizaos/plugin-video#build` has emitted `dist/index.js` but not `dist/index.d.ts`. Calendar currently traverses `@elizaos/agent` source, whose generated optional-plugin map imports Video, so TypeScript fails nondeterministically with TS7016.

# Scope

Add the missing package-specific Turbo ordering edge for Calendar typecheck. Do not add a Calendar to Video manifest dependency, suppress TS7016, or rely on retries. Remove the temporary edge in the later canonical Calendar slice after that slice eliminates the Calendar to Agent source coupling.

# Acceptance

- [ ] A clean workspace schedules Video build before Calendar typecheck.
- [ ] The exact affected typecheck command passes from a clean install.
- [ ] Turbo dependency audits and full repository verification pass.
- [ ] The final cumulative approved product tree remains unchanged after the canonical Calendar slice removes the now-unneeded edge.

# Reproduction

GitHub run 30956924035, job 92152052372: Calendar typecheck began before Video declaration generation completed and failed at `packages/agent/src/runtime/optional-plugin-imports.generated.ts`.

topIssues.title: [agent] fix(contribute-skill): support Ubuntu GitHub CLI pagination
topIssues.author: 0xSolace
topIssues.body:
## Project / Coordination

- Project board: N/A - contributor-skill tooling is repository infrastructure and is not routed through an active product board.
- Parent tracker or epic: N/A - standalone compatibility defect found while dogfooding the required contributor inventory.
- Coordination Discussion: N/A - scope and evidence remain on this issue and its PR.
- Suggested lane tag: sol-army-a

## Contribution Provenance

AI assistance is self-reported provenance, not a request for hidden reasoning.
Use the exact runtime values; do not include secrets, tokens, private prompts,
session IDs, or chain-of-thought.

- AI assistance: yes
- AI provider/model: openai-codex / gpt-5.6-sol
- Client / agent tooling: OpenClaw subagent
- Contribution skill revision: elizaOS/eliza@e37924817dd457f3c5cc1547531c7054336a3740:packages/skills/skills/contribute-to-eliza
- Attribution status: self-reported

## Scope

The contributor skill requires `live-report.mjs` before work selection, but its GitHub adapter invokes `gh api --slurp`. Ubuntu 24.04 currently packages GitHub CLI 2.45.0, whose `gh api` does not support `--slurp`, so the mandatory inventory exits before making its first read. The same compatibility gap was reproduced in two independent contributor-skill audits.

Replace the `--slurp` dependency with a pagination format supported by the repository's practical GitHub CLI baseline while preserving the adapter's GET-only and complete-pagination guarantees. Document the compatibility contract in the skill and keep malformed or partial output fail-closed. This scope must not edit workflows.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `live-report.mjs --repo elizaOS/eliza --json` completes with GitHub CLI 2.45.0.
- [ ] Every paginated request remains explicitly `--method GET`; no mutation verb can enter the adapter.
- [ ] Multi-page arrays are returned completely and in order, including empty-page and malformed-output handling.
- [ ] Spawn failures, nonzero exits, malformed records, and truncated output fail with actionable endpoint context.
- [ ] Deterministic tests cover success, multiple pages, empty results, malformed/truncated output, command failure, and GET-only invocation.
- [ ] The skill documents the supported pagination behavior without claiming an unsupported minimum GitHub CLI version.
- [ ] The real read-only inventory is run, its JSON opens successfully, and summary/candidate excerpts are manually inspected.

## Evidence Plan

- [ ] Screenshots or recording: N/A - CLI compatibility change has no rendered UI.
- [ ] Logs: attach the pre-fix unsupported-flag failure and post-fix live inventory transcript inline.
- [ ] Real-LLM trajectories: N/A - no model, prompt, provider, action, or agent runtime behavior changes.
- [ ] Domain artifacts: attach the post-fix machine-readable inventory summary and manually reviewed candidate excerpt.
- [ ] CI or local commands: focused contribution-skill tests, package build/typecheck/lint, repository `bun run verify`, and live `--json` inventory.

## Claim / Status Notes

topIssues.title: ci: fork-PR aggregate gates poll to timeout on checks held at action_required
topIssues.author: Zorba-the-buddhah
topIssues.body:
## Problem

On a fork PR from a first-time contributor, GitHub holds every
`pull_request`-triggered workflow at `action_required` until a maintainer
approves the run. Both aggregate gates trigger on `pull_request_target`, which is
exempt from that approval, so they start immediately and poll for checks that
cannot appear. After the full timeout budget they convert "never appeared" into
`FAILED`.

The result is a PR whose required checks are all red without any of them having
evaluated the diff, and roughly 20-40 minutes of runner time consumed per gate,
per PR, producing no signal.

## Evidence

Two PRs, different sizes, different subsystems, same failure:

| PR | Diff | Develop PR Gate | Security Advisory Gate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #17545 | +1206/-24, 17 files, `packages/cloud/shared` | FAILED | FAILED |
| #17546 | +356/-39, 2 files, Discord onboarding | FAILED | passed |

**Develop PR Gate** — [run 30701753824](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/30701753824),
81 polls over ~40 minutes:

```
poll 81: passed=0 waiting=0 failed=7
FAILED lint:               no GitHub Actions check run from .github/workflows/develop-pr.yml
FAILED typecheck:          no GitHub Actions check run from .github/workflows/develop-pr.yml
FAILED build:              no GitHub Actions check run from .github/workflows/develop-pr.yml
FAILED gitleaks:           no GitHub Actions check run from .github/workflows/gitleaks.yml
FAILED check-pr-evidence:  no GitHub Actions check run from .github/workflows/pr.yaml
FAILED check-pr-title:     no GitHub Actions check run from .github/workflows/pr.yaml
FAILED stale-base guard:   no GitHub Actions check run from .github/workflows/stale-base-guard.yml
```

**Security Advisory Gate** — [run 30701716047](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/30701716047),
~40 polls over 20 minutes:

```
waiting for deterministic security checks: gitleaks
...
scripts/security/security-advisory-gate.mjs:148
Error: timed out waiting for security advisory checks
```

Workflow run states on the same branch at that moment — none had started:

```
gitleaks         | completed | action_required | pull_request
Cloud Tests      | completed | action_required | pull_request
Develop PR       | completed | action_required | pull_request
Security Review  | completed | action_required | pull_request
Quality (Fork)   | completed | action_required | pull_request
… 13 workflows total
```

The Security Advisory Gate difference between the two PRs is scope, not health:
it did not require `gitleaks` for the smaller diff.

## Why the existing approval handling does not cover this

`security-advisory-gate.mjs` already models approval latency — `approvalDeadline`
plus `requiredChecksStartedBy()` grants a bounded completion grace when required
checks *started* before the deadline. That handles "approved, but slow".

It does not distinguish that from "held at `action_required`, so it will never
start". In the second case the wait cannot succeed by construction, but the gate
still consumes its whole budget before reporting a failure whose message
("timed out") does not name the actual cause.

## Suggested direction

Treat a required check whose workflow run is `action_required` as *not yet
approved* rather than *pending*:

- fail fast with an explicit message ("required workflows awaiting maintainer
  approval: …") instead of polling to exhaustion, or
- skip the gate for fork PRs until approval lands, letting it run on the
  post-approval re-run.

Either turns a silent 20-40 minute timeout into an immediate, actionable
statement, and stops burning runner capacity on a wait that cannot resolve. It
also stops a reviewer seeing seven red required checks that never ran.

Both gates share the shape, so whichever fix applies probably wants to apply to
both.

## Notes

- This is reported from the outside, based on two runs; if the current behaviour
  is deliberate — a gate cannot know a check will never arrive — feel free to
  close.
- I have not claimed this. Happy to pick it up if useful, though I cannot
  reproduce the `action_required` state on demand to verify a fix, so someone
  with repo-side visibility may be better placed.

topPRs.title: fix(i18n): restore the source catalog, purge dead keys, and wire the catalog checker into CI
topPRs.author: ss251
topPRs.body:
Closes #17605 `en.json` is the source catalog every other locale keys off — and it had drifted **705 keys behind source**, because the strict checker built to prevent exactly that (`packages/scripts/check-i18n.mjs`) was invoked from **no CI lane, no package script, nothing**. `defaultValue` masked every miss for English users, which is why it rotted silently; all seven non-English locales render English for those strings and could never translate them. The reverse rot accumulated too: **469 dead keys** (referenced by no literal, no source template prefix, no allowlist entry) sat in every locale, plus one key translated in all seven locales that never existed in en and is used nowhere. ## Commit 1 — catalog repair (locale JSONs only) - **703 entries restored** to `en.json`, each value extracted **verbatim from its call site's inline `defaultValue`** (zero conflicting defaults across duplicate sites — no invented copy; byte-for-byte what English users already see). Pure line insertions: `703 insertions(+), 0 deletions(-)` on the file's existing formatting. - **3,741 dead lines purged** across all eight locales (the 469 dead keys everywhere they existed + the seven-locale orphan `mediagalleryview.SearchActive`). Pure line removals; every file re-parsed after edit. Each deletion is checker-derived: uncovered by literals AND source template prefixes AND the allowlist. - The 2 remaining source-missing keys (`settings.cloudOverview.localModeLabel`/`Description`) pass **runtime-conditional** defaults (ternaries on cloud-connection state). Cataloging them would freeze one branch and silently change rendered English (catalog wins over `defaultValue`), and splitting them is a `packages/ui` surface change requiring visual evidence — deliberately out of scope. They are declared, with reasons, in the new `uncatalogued` allowlist field, and the checker fails if such an entry ever outlives its call site. ## Commit 2 — make the checker wireable, then wire it The old contract (any locale missing any key = error) made the gate permanently red — presumably why it ended up wired nowhere. New contract, aligned with what CI can hold on every PR: - **Errors**: literal key missing from the source locale; unused source-locale key; orphaned translation (locale key absent from source); stale `uncatalogued` entry. - **Warnings** (errors under `--strict-translations`): non-source locales missing used keys / lagging the source catalog — translation debt stays *visible* on every run without blocking unrelated PRs. - `runI18nCheck` exported pure (no console/exit) with **10 fixture tests** covering each failure mode red and green, following the `ci-bun-version-contract` test pattern; the real-repo test asserts `ok:true` **and** that translation-gap warnings are present (a silent pass would hide the backfill the same way the unwired checker did). - Wired into `test.yml` beside the other contracts, so no new key can ship uncataloged again. ## Proof (verbatim)
before → after ``` $ node packages/scripts/check-i18n.mjs; echo exit=$? # develop, before [i18n] en.json missing 705 key(s) used in source: - cloud.account.securityLink (packages/ui/src/cloud/account-security/AccountPage.tsx:37) … exit=1 $ grep -rn "check-i18n" package.json packages/*/package.json .github/workflows/*.yml # develop, before (no results — the checker was invoked from nowhere) $ node packages/scripts/check-i18n.mjs; echo exit=$? # this branch [i18n] es.json is missing 830 translation(s) of en.json keys (falls back to en at runtime) … (7 warning lines, one per non-source locale) [i18n] OK — 4519 literal keys, 6 wildcard prefixes, 76 dynamic sites; 7709 source keys × 8 locales exit=0 $ bun test packages/scripts/__tests__/check-i18n.test.ts 10 pass 0 fail 22 expect() calls $ bunx biome check packages/scripts/check-i18n.mjs packages/scripts/__tests__/check-i18n.test.ts Checked 2 files.
